answer: Tie each agent identity to a cryptographic cipher binding it to one human-verified credential, then let reputation grow like a vine: endorsements chain back to known root agents, each link sealed by a time-stamped attestation that costs real computation or a scarce fee. An attacker can spawn thousands of fake identities, but those sybils can only wander the shallow edges of the trust graph — they cannot forge deep vines, since every genuine link costs something. Markets then quarantine shallow-rooted identities while deep chains trade freely.
